problem.text: In the diagram below, $ABCD$ is a square. Point $E$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AD}$. Points $F$ and $G$ lie on $\overline{CE}$, and $H$ and $J$ lie on $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{BC}$, respectively, so that $FGHJ$ is a square. Points $K$ and $L$ lie on $\overline{GH}$, and $M$ and $N$ lie on $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{AB}$, respectively, so that $KLMN$ is a square. The area of $KLMN$ is $99$. Find the area of $FGHJ$.

steps.title: Where to start: the midpoint fixes the shape of triangle $DCE$
steps.body: Every side of both small squares is parallel or perpendicular to $CE$, so the same angle keeps appearing in the corner triangles. The clue is that $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$: if the big square has side $s$, then right triangle $DCE$ has legs $DE = \frac{s}{2}$ and $DC = s$, in ratio $1 : 2$. Let $a = \angle DCE$.

your_turn.prompt: Find the hypotenuse $CE$ in terms of $s$, and write the three sides of $\triangle DCE$ as a ratio.

steps.title: Five similar right triangles
steps.body: Chasing angles around the figure, the angle $a$ appears at $\angle DCE$, $\angle FJC$, $\angle BHJ$, $\angle KNH$ and $\angle AMN$, so the right triangles $DCE$, $FJC$, $BHJ$, $KNH$, $AMN$ are all similar. In each one, the leg opposite angle $a$ : the leg next to it : the hypotenuse $= 1 : 2 : \sqrt5$. Careful: in each triangle find which leg is opposite $a$ before using the ratio.

your_turn.answer: $\angle FCJ = 90^\circ - a$ because $\angle DCB = 90^\circ$. Triangle $FJC$ has a right angle at $F$, so its third angle $\angle FJC$ is $a$.

steps.title: Use the small square on side $AB$
steps.body: Square $KLMN$ has area $99$, so $MN = NK = \sqrt{99} = 3\sqrt{11}$. In $\triangle AMN$ the hypotenuse is $MN$ and $AN$ is opposite $a$ (at $M$), so $AN = \frac{3\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt5} = \frac{3\sqrt{55}}{5}$. In $\triangle KNH$ the angle $a$ is at $N$, so $NK$ is the longer leg and $NH$ is the hypotenuse.

steps.title: Use the big square $FGHJ$
steps.body: Let the side of $FGHJ$ be $x$. In $\triangle BHJ$ the hypotenuse is $HJ = x$ and $a$ is at $H$, so $BJ = \frac{x}{\sqrt5} = \frac{x\sqrt5}{5}$ and $HB = \frac{2x\sqrt5}{5}$. In $\triangle FJC$ the angle $a$ is at $J$, so $JF = x$ is the longer leg and $JC$ is the hypotenuse.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Side $AB = AN + NH + HB$ and side $BC = BJ + JC$ are equal:
$$\frac{3\sqrt{55}}{5} + \frac{3\sqrt{55}}{2} + \frac{2x\sqrt5}{5} = \frac{x\sqrt5}{5} + \frac{x\sqrt5}{2}.$$
This simplifies to $\frac{21\sqrt{55}}{10} = \frac{3x\sqrt5}{10}$, so $x = 7\sqrt{11}$ and the area of $FGHJ$ is $x^2 = 49 \cdot 11 = 539$. The answer is **$539$**.
